c: Hamilcar took the army which he had led in the Mercenary War to Iberia in 237 BC and carved out a quasi-monarchicial, autonomous state in its south east.

t: Varro and Aemilius Paullus elected consuls
c: In the 216 BC elections Terentius Varro and Aemilius Paullus were elected as consuls; both were more aggressively minded than Fabius.
Fabius was elected consul in 215 BC and re-elected in 214 BC.

t: Philip V pledges support to Hannibal
c: During 216 BC the Macedonian king, Philip V, pledged his support to Hannibal, initiating the First Macedonian War against Rome in 215 BC.

t: Hasdrubal Barca crosses Alps into Italy
c: In the spring of 207 BC Hasdrubal Barca repeated the feat of his elder brother by marching an army of 35,000 men across the Alps and invading Italy.

t: Mago lands in Genua with Spanish army
c: In 205 BC Mago landed in Genua (modern Genoa) in north-west Italy with the remnants of his Spanish army where it received Gallic and Ligurian reinforcements.

t: Scipio arrives in Iberia with reinforcements
c: In 210 BC Publius Cornelius Scipio arrived in Iberia with further Roman reinforcements.

t: Battle of Baecula between Hasdrubal and Scipio
c: In the spring of 208 BC Hasdrubal moved to engage Scipio at the battle of Baecula.

t: Scipio defeats Carthaginians at battle of Ilipa
c: In 206 BC at the battle of Ilipa, Scipio with 48,000 men, half Italian and half Iberian, defeated a Carthaginian army of 54,500 men and 32 elephants.

t: Scipio given command of legions in Sicily
c: In 205 BC Publius Scipio was given command of the legions in Sicily and allowed to enrol volunteers for his plan to end the war by an invasion of Africa.

t: Hannibal persuades Carthage to accept peace treaty
c: Many senior Carthaginians wanted to reject it, but Hannibal spoke strongly in its favour and it was accepted in spring 201 BC.

t: Scipio Aemilianus elected consul of Africa

t: Romans secure foothold near Carthage harbour
c: In the spring of 146 BC the Roman army managed to secure a foothold on the fortifications near the harbour.

t: Rome and Carthage sign symbolic peace treaty
c: In 1985, a symbolic peace treaty and pact of friendship was signed between the mayors of Rome and Carthage.

t: First Punic War ends in Roman victory
c: The First Punic War had ended in a Roman victory in 241 BC after 23 years and enormous losses on both sides.
Moving to southern Italy in 216 Hannibal defeated the Romans again at the battle of Cannae, where he annihilated the largest army the Romans had ever assembled.

t: Carthaginians attempt to capture Sicily and Sardinia
c: Between 215 and 210 BC the Carthaginians attempted to capture Roman-held Sicily and Sardinia, but were unsuccessful.

t: Hannibal seizes supply depot at Cannae
c: In the spring of 216 BC Hannibal seized the large supply depot at Cannae on the Apulian plain.

In 211 BC Rome contained the Macedonians by allying with the Aetolian League, a coalition of Greek city states which was already at war with Macedonia.

t: Rebellion on Sardinia crushed by Romans
c: A rebellion in support of the Carthaginians broke out on Sardinia in 213 BC, but it was quickly put down by the Romans.

t: Hannibal offers battle to Roman forces
c: In 211 BC Hannibal again offered battle to the besieging Roman forces, this time they declined to leave their fortifications.

t: Mago Barca lands in Genua with Spanish army
c: In 205 BC, Mago Barca, another of Hannibal's younger brothers, landed in Genua in north-west Italy with the remnants of his Spanish army.

t: Hasdrubal ordered to reinforce Hannibal in Italy
c: In 216 Hasdrubal received orders from Carthage to move into Italy and join up with Hannibal to put pressure on the Romans in their homeland.

t: Claudius Nero stabilises situation in Iberia
c: Claudius Nero brought over reinforcements in 210 BC and stabilised the situation.
In 203 BC Carthage succeeded in recruiting at least 4,000 mercenaries from Iberia, despite Rome's nominal control.

t: Carthage divides Numidian kingdoms with Syphax
c: In 206 BC the Carthaginians ended this drain on their resources by dividing several Numidian kingdoms with Syphax.

t: Roman camp relocated to healthier location
c: 149 BC – The camp established by Censorinus was badly situated and by early summer was so pestiferous that it was moved to a healthier location.
147 BC – Once this feature was complete, Scipio detached a large force and led it against the Carthaginian field army at Nepheris.
146 BC – 50,000 Carthaginian prisoners were sold into slavery.

t: Second Punic War ends with peace treaty
c: When the Second Punic War ended in 201 BC one of the terms of the peace treaty prohibited Carthage from waging war without Rome's permission.

t: Hannibal Mago leads second expedition to Sicily
c: In retaliation Hannibal Mago led a second Carthaginian expedition in 406 BC.

t: Mago II defeated near Abacaenum by Dionysius
c: In 393 BC, Mago II, successor of Himilco, led an attack on Messina, but was defeated near Abacaenum by Dionysius.

t: Dionysius II makes peace with Carthage
c: After his death in 367 BC, his son Dionysius II made peace with Carthage, and Carthage retained her Sicilian possessions west of the Halycas and Himera rivers.
